question: A key activity of the European Defence Agency is the regular development of capability planning scenarios to support future investments to strengthen our armed forces. These capability planning scenarios are based on input from Member States and should be coherent with other European defence initiatives such as PESCO, CARD and the 2010 Headline Goal. The Strategic Compass calls for a review of this Headline Goal process by 2023, but little has been communicated in this regard to date. 1.
Can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy confirm whether this revision is still under consideration?
Will subsequent capability planning scenarios take account of NATO initiatives in this regard, more specifically the NATO Defence Planning Process?
answer: The Strategic Compass (1) sets the objective that by 2023, the Headline Goal process (HLGP) would be revised, and military capability development would be brought closer to operational needs, also given the HLGP’s essential contribution to the Capability Development Plan (CDP). Since its inception in 2008, the CDP has been prepared under the lead of the European Defence Agency (EDA).

The CDP was revised, and the 2023 Capability Development Priorities were agreed at the EDA Steering Board in November 2023 (2). The Strategic Compass also sets the objective to develop, by mid-2022, detailed strategic planning elements to adapt the capability planning scenarios. In June 2022, the Political and Security Committee approved the Detailed Orientations for the next HLGP cycle (2023-2026) (3).

The five capability planning scenarios under HLGP (peace enforcement, conflict prevention, support to stabilisation and capacity building, rescue and evacuation, support to humanitarian assistance and disaster relief) were revised by spring 2023, under the EU Military Committee’s lead with the support of the EU Military Staff.

They were included in the Requirements Catalogue (RC 23), approved by the Council in January 2024 (4), which defines the EU’s requirements for capabilities. The EU CDP, the HLGP and the Coordinated Annual Review on Defence are coherent in output with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation’s Defence Planning Process.
